Name: Apolitical / Not Systematically Political
Description: Philosophers who did not develop a systematic political theory or were primarily focused outside of politics.

Name: Liberal
Description: Political thought centered on individual rights, limited government, and freedom of thought, speech, and commerce.

Name: Monarchist / Elitist / Advises Rulers
Description: Political thought favoring rule by a monarch or qualified elite, often taking the form of advice offered to rulers.

Name: Democratic / Republican
Description: Political thought favoring self-government, popular sovereignty, and constitutional or republican forms of rule.

Name: Religious / Theocratic
Description: Political thought grounding legitimate authority in religious law, doctrine, or ecclesiastical institutions.

Name: Radical Left / Revolutionary
Description: Political thought favoring fundamental, often revolutionary transformation of existing social and economic structures.

Name: Socialist / Social Democratic
Description: Political thought favoring collective ownership, economic redistribution, and a strong social welfare state.

Name: Anti-authoritarian / Anti-totalitarian
Description: Political thought centrally concerned with resisting authoritarian, fascist, or totalitarian concentrations of power.

Name: Reformist / Moderate
Description: Political thought favoring gradual, incremental improvement of existing institutions rather than revolution or radical change.

Name: Cosmopolitan / Globalist
Description: Political thought favoring international or global forms of community, justice, and obligation beyond the nation-state.

Name: Authoritarian / Strong State
Description: Political thought favoring a strong, centralized state with extensive power over social and individual life.

Name: Communist / Marxist
Description: Political thought favoring the abolition of private property and class society along Marxist lines.

Name: Anti-colonial / Pan-African
Description: Political thought centered on resisting colonialism and imperialism and on African political unity and self-determination.

Name: Feminist / Queer Politics
Description: Political thought centered on gender equality and the critique of patriarchal and heteronormative power structures.

Name: Communitarian / Critical of Liberalism
Description: Political thought emphasizing community, tradition, and shared goods against what it sees as excessive liberal individualism.

Name: Political Realism
Description: Political thought emphasizing the practical realities of power over idealized moral or institutional theorizing.

Name: Libertarian
Description: Political thought favoring minimal government and maximal individual liberty, especially in economic life.

Name: Cultural Nationalist
Description: Political thought centered on the cultural distinctiveness and self-determination of a particular nation or people.
